newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - July 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - July 15.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. For further information on these articles or details of BMC's other international press and broadcast services call Simon McMillan on +44 (0)171 256 5130 or e-mail bmc.co@ft.com.
-- BOEING AND EU CLOSER TO DEAL

US aircraft giant Boeing held a meeting with the European Commission on Monday in hopes of reaching an agreement that would help break the deal between it and McDonnell Douglas. The Commission reportedly will accept the deal if Boeing agrees to licence a third party to manufacture spare parts for McDonnell Douglas' civilian aircraft. The Commission had expressed concern that if the merger went ahead on its original terms, Boeing would have possessed an 'overwhelming' position in the civil aircraft market, hampering competition.
-- BT FACES GRILLING BY INVESTORS OVER MCI LOSSES

British Telecom chairman Sir Iain Vallance is expected to face a 'flood' of questioning from shareholders at the group's annual general meeting in Edinburgh on Wednesday over the future of the company's planned merger with MCI. Following the AGM, BT director in charge of international alliance Robert Brace will fly to Washington to take a closer look at MCI's strategy and problems in breaking the US local telephone market. Brace will be joined by BT chief executive Peter Bonfield for the MCI review.
-- BA GROUND STAFF LEADERS AGREE TO SEEK NEW TALKS

British Airways' chief executive Robert Ayling has welcomed the decision by leaders of the 9,000 strong BA ground staff to seek fresh talks rather than proceed with the strike. Ayling declared it was the company's intention all along to continue talks with employees and their unions in order to ensure BA 'protected their interests in the transfer to the new business'. Union leaders have drawn up proposals for achieving the 42 million stg in savings being sought by the airline. They will be submitted later this week.
-- VAT RECEIPT SHAKE-UP MAY SAVE GROUP 1 BN STG

A ruling by Customs & Exchange which approves the use of electric payment card receipts for VAT calculations will save the top 1,000 UK companies one billion stg through the elimination of purchasing paperwork. The C&E decision follows trials by card consortium Visa who teamed up with three member banks and a 25 purchasers and suppliers in a bid to prove to customs its systems were as reliable as a paper invoice. Germany has already approved the method, and Visa is now looking into France, Belgium, Ireland and Switzerland.
-- CHIRAC WARNS JOSPIN NOT TO HINDER INDUSTRY

French president Jacques Chirac has warned the country's Socialist government it should resume reforms initiated by Alain Juppe, including calls to make it more difficult to lay off employees, so that industry would not be hampered by 'obsolete and absurd regulations'. Chirac also advised the prime minister to slow down the country's rate of privatisation. The government responded that Chirac negl ected to realise 'on June 1, the French rejected the choices, decisions and measures' of the prior government and reaffirmed France's commitment to join Emu, despite its 3.5 percent budget deficit.
-- LLOYD'S MAY RESTRICT BUSINESS HELD BY AGENCIES

Lloyd's of London, expressing concern over the rapid consolidation among managing agencies, are reported to be considering limiting the amount of business controlled by the agencies managing its insurance syndicates. Andrew Duguid, head of policy and planning at Lloyd's, has suggested the company put 15 percent of its overall capacity as a 'starting point' in looking at the maximum amount of a business any company should control.
-- MPS SET FOR LAST ASSAULT ON WINDFALL TAX

The Labour government will face its final challenge over the windfall tax on Tuesday, as shadow chancellor Peter Lilley will attack the tax for its levies on companies that have not benefited from any windfall profits. The Tory party will propose the tax be imposed on shareholders who made gains in the last six months after flotation, and will back complaints made by groups such as Welsh water and electricity company Hyder and Northern Electric, who believe the tax is being unfairly levied on them.
-- GERMANY SPEEDS UP LUFTHANSA SELL-OFF

The German transport ministry has said that the sale of the government's remaining 35.68 percent stake in national airline Lufthansa is likely to take place in October or November. The comments follow an invitation by the German government to seven international banks for their proposals to arrange the privatisation of the stake, which is expected to raise up to DM2.4 billion.
-- POWERGEN LOOKS TO EXPAND

UK electricity generator PowerGen has indicated that it intends to link up with regional electricity companies after admitting that its 203 million stg windfall tax bill was much less than expected. Speaking at the group's annual meeting, chairman Ed Wallis suggested that PowerGen could link-up with some of the US energy groups that had bought regional electricity companies in the UK.
-- EUROMONEY STILL TEMPTED BY US PRESS GROUP

UK magazine and exhibitions group Euromoney has confirmed it is still interested in acquiring Institutional Investor, the US press group. The American group, which is being sold by Walt Disney, had been involved in talks with Pearson, but the UK media group pulled out last month. Euromoney had also been reported to have withdrawn from talks because of the high price, but the group's finance director Colin Jones said Monday they are still interested.
